Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin for metastatic soft tissue sarcomaNational Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) 00205

Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

These are patient-language severity prompts, not a validated questionnaire or a formal Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading tool. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Serious symptoms override the columns: call without waiting to decide a severity level.
Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

Eribulin for unresectable liposarcomaNational Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) 00228

Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

These are patient-language severity prompts, not a validated questionnaire or a formal Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading tool. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Serious symptoms override the columns: call without waiting to decide a severity level.
Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

A port is a small chamber beneath the skin, usually on the chest, attached to a tube ending in a large vein. A special needle goes through the skin into the port when it is used. Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

Vinblastine and methotrexate for aggressive fibromatosisNational Cancer Control Programme (NCCP) 00554

Record each cycle separately. Each medicine has its own symptom table. Mark the worst symptoms since your last review, when they occurred and what they stopped you doing. Overlapping symptoms can be recorded under more than one medicine; you do not have to identify the cause.

These are patient-language severity prompts, not a validated questionnaire or a formal Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading tool. Your team assigns the clinical grade. Serious symptoms override the columns: call without waiting to decide a severity level.
Use a new record sheet for each cycle or review. Copy or print another sheet when needed; the number of sheets does not prescribe the length of treatment.

Vinblastine interferes with microtubules, preventing cells from dividing normally. Blood production, bowel movement and nerves may also be affected. It is given only into a vein by trained staff; other administration routes can be fatal.

The likelihood and severity differ between medicines and people. Use this general discussion together with every medicine-specific risk below.

Discuss realistic benefit, uncertainty, alternatives including observation or symptom-focused care when appropriate, serious and lasting risks, personal priorities and the option to decline or reconsider treatment. This injected regimen gives three weekly doses followed by a one-week break, for up to 12 cycles. Follow the written injection calendar; never substitute daily oral methotrexate. Desmoid treatment is outside the listed licensed indications of the examined vinblastine and methotrexate products. The national regimen supports this use; your team should explain the product-specific off-label rationale and document consent under local policy.

A small historical phase II study using methotrexate 30 mg/m² and vinblastine 6 mg/m² weekly found tumour shrinkage or stability and symptom benefit in some patients with advanced inoperable aggressive fibromatosis. It supports activity but had no randomised comparator.

The study used continuous weekly treatment, rather than the current National Cancer Control Programme days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle. DESMOPAZ used vinblastine 5 mg/m² and a different weekly-then-fortnightly schedule; its non-comparative randomised design does not establish a definitive head-to-head superiority result. Do not present trial rates as validated estimates for this exact schedule.
